Dearest Traveler,

I write to you from Chugoku, a land carved by calm seas and silent winds. Here, on the island of Miyajima, the great red Torii gate stands tall in the ocean water. When the tide rises, the gate appears to float, suspended between the blue sea and the green mountains, a bridge between our world and the divine.

In Hiroshima, the silent paper cranes piled high at the Peace Memorial whisper of hope, resilience, and the gentle strength of peace. Further north, the giant sand dunes of Tottori meet the roaring Sea of Japan, dynamic and ever-shifting. Chugoku reminds us that even when the tides of life are high, we must remain standing, beautiful and at peace.

In quiet contemplation,
Kokoro of Chugoku
